title: Wildfires spread in France and Spain forcing more to flee
facts: Wildfires forced resident evacuations near Bordeaux in France and Madrid in Spain.
A wildfire near the Spanish coastal town of Valencia caused one fatality.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stated that wildfires in the Gironde region intensified overnight.
French authorities deployed 2,500 firefighters, 1,500 military personnel, and 1,200 police officers to the Gironde region.
Total wildfire-related evacuations across France exceeded 220,000 people.
Wildfires near Bordeaux forced the closure of an Atlantic coast highway and interrupted regional rail services.
The city of Bordeaux has a population of approximately 268,000 residents.
Wildfires in France burned approximately 42,000 hectares (103,000 acres) of land.
The burned area in France represents the highest total since 1949, when 50,000 hectares were destroyed.
Firefighters in the southern French department of Var battled a separate wildfire that prompted 3,000 evacuations.
Wildfires burned areas to the west and north of the Spanish capital Madrid.
Spanish authorities mandated the evacuation of eight municipalities located near Toledo.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez conducted a tour of fire-affected areas west of Madrid.
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez reported positive progress in overnight containment efforts in Spain.
The 42,000 hectares burned in France equal an area roughly four times the size of Paris.
